title: English Vocabulary 4 · Units 99–100
description: Gender-aware English, inclusive occupational terms, terms of address and gendered connotations; the specialised compressed language of press headlines, sensational word choice and newspaper puns.
sourceNotice: Prepared for personal study using the user-supplied textbook. Vocabulary choices and meaning distinctions follow the teaching pages, exercises and answer key; all explanations, examples and Brazilian Portuguese translations were written independently, without reproducing source passages or exercises.

audit.scope: Unit 99 sections A–B, gender-neutral alternatives, register and exercises 99.1–99.4; Unit 100 sections A–C, headline grammar, emotional vocabulary and wordplay exercises 100.1–100.3; corresponding answer key.
audit.pronunciation: Selective broad British IPA is included for short items where confidently established; blank IPA means not checked to a sufficient standard. MP3 files are not included. Normal word audio reads the word field, while examples remain separate sentence-audio text.
audit.languagePolicy: All learner-facing explanatory content and metadata are in English; natural Brazilian Portuguese translations appear only in pt fields.
audit.reviewMethod: Compared the full four book pages, embedded tables, notes and exercises with the relevant answer-key pages. Independently reviewed meaning and connotation, register, provenance, contemporary gender-neutral usage qualifications, examples and pronunciations, followed by saved-JSON structural and audio-target lint checks.
audit.limitations: This package contains no MP3 audio. Real browser import, TTS playback and pronunciation-recognition tests in VocabLab have not been run. The textbook is a 2017 edition; some discussion of gender-neutral usage reflects debates at that time and is contextualised in notes. Tabloid style is primarily for reading comprehension rather than imitation in formal writing.

units.title: Unit 99 — Language and gender
units.source: Vocabulary study targets from published reference material; Unit 99. Page information, if available, is retained in sourceAudit.
units.category: Language and society · gender-aware vocabulary, address and register
learningObjectives: Recognise gender-specific and gender-neutral occupational terms without assuming all occupational titles are interchangeable.
Use Ms, Miss and Mrs with appropriate awareness of marital-status implications and personal preferences.
Distinguish male and female from masculine and feminine, and interpret colloquial guy, bloke, lad, laddish, girlfriend and macho.
Understand generic masculine usage, inclusive alternatives and singular they while preserving the textbook context.

sectionsChecked: A · Gender awareness and vocabulary, terminology table, historical usage discussion and footnotes
B · Words referring to men and women, usage notes, connotations and examples
Exercises 99.1–99.4 and answer-key notes on alternatives and pronouns

items.pt: linguagem neutra em relação a gênero
items.section: A · Gender-aware and gender-neutral vocabulary
items.example: The university revised its recruitment materials to use gender-neutral language.
items.note: Language that does not unnecessarily identify one gender as the default; usage varies by context and audience.

items.pt: linguagem com viés de gênero
items.section: A · Gender-aware and gender-neutral vocabulary
items.example: The editor highlighted gender-biased language in the job advertisement.
items.note: Language reflecting or reinforcing assumptions about gender; discussed in the unit's rationale and exercises.

items.word: male words with a generic meaning
items.pt: palavras masculinas usadas para se referir a pessoas em geral
items.section: A · Gender-aware and gender-neutral vocabulary
items.example: The phrase used male words with a generic meaning even when referring to everyone.
items.note: Refers to masculine-coded terms used for mixed or unspecified groups, not specifically to male people.

items.pt: sentido genérico; significado abrangente
items.section: A · Gender-aware and gender-neutral vocabulary
items.example: In older manuals, a masculine pronoun sometimes had a generic meaning.
items.note: Generic means referring to a category as a whole rather than to a specific individual.

items.pt: presidente de comissão; ocupante da presidência, na terminologia tradicional
items.section: A · Gender-aware and gender-neutral vocabulary
items.example: The minutes of the older meeting referred to the committee chair as chairman.
items.note: Traditional term historically used generically; chair and chairperson are neutral alternatives.

items.pt: presidente de reunião ou comissão; pessoa que preside
items.section: A · Gender-aware and gender-neutral vocabulary
items.example: The chair invited members to ask questions before the vote.
items.note: A gender-neutral title for the person presiding over a meeting or committee; also means a seat in other contexts.

items.pt: pessoa que preside; presidente de reunião ou comissão
items.section: A · Gender-aware and gender-neutral vocabulary
items.example: The chairperson closed the meeting after the final agenda item.
items.note: Gender-neutral alternative to chairman, generally interchangeable with chair in this sense.

items.pt: porta-voz
items.section: A · Gender-aware and gender-neutral vocabulary
items.example: A spokesperson confirmed that the exhibition would open on Monday.
items.note: Neutral counterpart to spokesman or spokeswoman, especially for official statements.

items.pt: bombeiro; profissional de combate a incêndios
items.section: A · Gender-aware and gender-neutral vocabulary
items.example: Firefighters evacuated the building before the smoke spread.
items.note: Neutral occupational label rather than fireman; it names the job without identifying gender.

items.pt: policial; agente da polícia
items.section: A · Gender-aware and gender-neutral vocabulary
items.example: A police officer took a statement from the witness.
items.note: Neutral occupational expression replacing the generic use of policeman.

items.pt: comissário de bordo; comissária de bordo
items.section: A · Gender-aware and gender-neutral vocabulary
items.example: The flight attendant helped a passenger find a seat.
items.note: Neutral term used instead of air hostess or stewardess for cabin staff.

items.pt: profissional da limpeza; faxineiro ou faxineira
items.section: A · Gender-aware and gender-neutral vocabulary
items.example: The office employs a cleaner who comes in before opening time.
items.note: Job label without the gender assumption conveyed by cleaning lady.

items.pt: supervisor; responsável pela equipe
items.section: A · Gender-aware and gender-neutral vocabulary
items.example: The shift supervisor arranged cover for the absent employees.
items.note: Suggested as a neutral alternative to foreman; the precise authority and responsibilities may vary.

items.pt: atendente de vendas; vendedor de loja
items.section: A · Gender-aware and gender-neutral vocabulary
items.example: A sales assistant helped the customer compare two jackets.
items.note: Gender-neutral alternative to salesman in retail contexts; the exact job title varies by role.

items.pt: artificial; feito por processos humanos
items.section: A · Gender-aware and gender-neutral vocabulary
items.example: The bag was made from artificial fibres rather than natural cotton.
items.note: Useful neutral alternative to man-made for materials; artificial can have different connotations depending on context.

items.pt: a humanidade; a espécie humana
items.section: A · Gender-aware and gender-neutral vocabulary
items.example: The museum exhibition explored technological achievements of the human race.
items.note: Neutral alternative to mankind; human beings is another alternative.

items.pt: seres humanos; pessoas
items.section: A · Gender-aware and gender-neutral vocabulary
items.example: All human beings need access to safe drinking water.
items.note: Inclusive alternative to mankind, often more natural when referring to individual people collectively.

items.pt: manter uma central de atendimento com profissionais
items.section: A · Gender-aware and gender-neutral vocabulary
items.example: Volunteers will staff the helpline during the summer holidays.
items.note: Staff is a verb meaning provide people to operate a service; compare traditional man the helpline.

items.pt: a pessoa comum; o cidadão comum
items.section: A · Gender-aware and gender-neutral vocabulary
items.example: The person in the street may not know the details of the proposed reform.
items.note: Gender-neutral variant of the traditional idiom man in the street; the average person is another option.

items.pt: o cidadão comum; a pessoa comum, na formulação tradicional
items.section: A · Gender-aware and gender-neutral vocabulary
items.example: The columnist questioned whether the man in the street would support the measure.
items.note: Traditional generic expression; some speakers prefer the person in the street or the average person.

items.pt: tratar com brutalidade; agarrar ou empurrar com força
items.section: A · Gender-aware and gender-neutral vocabulary
items.example: Security staff were accused of trying to manhandle a peaceful protester.
items.note: Means handle someone roughly and forcefully; the book notes disagreement about removing man from established word forms.

items.pt: estado civil
items.section: A · Gender-aware and gender-neutral vocabulary
items.example: Applicants do not have to reveal their marital status on this form.
items.note: Refers to whether someone is married, single, divorced, etc.; distinct from gender.

items.pt: tratamento usado antes do sobrenome de uma mulher, sem indicar estado civil
items.section: A · Gender-aware and gender-neutral vocabulary
items.example: Ms Patel will lead the discussion at tomorrow's seminar.
items.note: Written title pronounced /mɪz/; unlike Miss and Mrs, it does not encode marital status.

items.pt: senhorita; tratamento tradicional para mulher não casada
items.section: A · Gender-aware and gender-neutral vocabulary
items.example: Miss Carter was the form of address used in the historical letter.
items.note: Traditionally indicates an unmarried woman; today many women prefer Ms regardless of marital status.

items.pt: senhora; tratamento tradicional para mulher casada
items.section: A · Gender-aware and gender-neutral vocabulary
items.example: Mrs Gomez asked the school to update her contact details.
items.note: Conventionally used for a married woman; pronunciation is /ˈmɪsɪz/, and preferences vary.

items.pt: macho; masculino, em classificação biológica
items.section: B · Words referring to men and women
items.example: The researchers recorded whether each bee was male or female.
items.note: Used for sex classification in biological contexts; not equivalent to masculine when describing style or behaviour.

items.pt: fêmea; feminino, em classificação biológica
items.section: B · Words referring to men and women
items.example: The female birds were slightly smaller than the males.
items.note: Biological classification; contrast with feminine, which concerns culturally associated traits or style.

items.pt: masculino; associado culturalmente ao masculino
items.section: B · Words referring to men and women
items.example: The costume featured traditionally masculine styling.
items.note: Describes traits or appearances conventionally regarded as male; avoid treating such associations as universal.

items.pt: feminino; associado culturalmente ao feminino
items.section: B · Words referring to men and women
items.example: The reviewer described the delicate design as feminine.
items.note: Describes culturally associated style or qualities, not necessarily the sex of the person or animal.

items.pt: cara; sujeito, em linguagem informal
items.section: B · Words referring to men and women
items.example: He's a friendly guy who always volunteers to help newcomers.
items.note: Informal word for a man in the singular; guys in group address can have a broader use.

items.pt: cara; sujeito, em inglês britânico informal
items.section: B · Words referring to men and women
items.example: I spoke to a bloke from the maintenance team outside the station.
items.note: Informal British-English word for a man; more regionally marked than guy.

items.pt: vocês; pessoal, em tratamento informal
items.section: B · Words referring to men and women
items.example: Are you guys ready to leave for the concert?
items.note: Often used informally for a mixed group, but not everyone regards it as fully gender-neutral.

items.pt: amiga próxima; namorada, conforme o contexto
items.section: B · Words referring to men and women
items.example: She was having lunch with two girlfriends from university.
items.note: The unit illustrates women using girlfriends for female friends; the same word can mean a romantic partner.

items.pt: de menina; associado a atividades estereotipicamente femininas
items.section: B · Words referring to men and women
items.example: They planned a girly evening with films and make-up.
items.note: Informal and stereotype-dependent; girly can be appreciative or dismissive depending on tone.

items.pt: rapaz; jovem, em inglês britânico informal
items.section: B · Words referring to men and women
items.example: A few lads were playing football in the park.
items.note: Informal British term for a boy or young man; often appears in the plural lads.

items.pt: típico de rapazes em grupo; com comportamento juvenil grosseiro
items.section: B · Words referring to men and women
items.example: The manager criticised the team's laddish jokes at the event.
items.note: Often disapproving, associated with rowdy or immature behaviour attributed to groups of young men.

items.pt: machão; que ostenta uma imagem de força masculina
items.section: B · Words referring to men and women
items.example: His macho image made it hard for him to admit he felt anxious.
items.note: Usually highlights conspicuous toughness or reluctance to express emotion; may be critical.

items.pt: a pessoa comum; o cidadão médio
items.section: Exercises · Inclusive usage and pronouns
items.example: The average person may find this scientific report difficult to interpret.
items.note: Plain neutral alternative to the man in the street; explicitly supplied by the unit's answer key.

items.pt: estereotipação de gênero; atribuição de papéis estereotipados a gêneros
items.section: Exercises · Inclusive usage and pronouns
items.example: The campaign aims to reduce gender stereotyping in school materials.
items.note: Names the practice of assigning fixed characteristics or roles to people based on gender.

items.pt: they no singular; pronome neutro para uma pessoa
items.section: Exercises · Inclusive usage and pronouns
items.example: If an employee has a concern, they should contact their manager.
items.note: The answer key acknowledges generic their; singular they is broadly accepted in current English and avoids guessing a person's gender.

items.pt: dele ou dela; forma explícita para dois pronomes possessivos
items.section: Exercises · Inclusive usage and pronouns
items.example: Each candidate should bring his or her passport to the interview.
items.note: Older inclusive alternative to generic his; singular their is often smoother, particularly for unknown gender.

units.title: Unit 100 — In the headlines
units.source: Vocabulary study targets from published reference material; Unit 100. Page information, if available, is retained in sourceAudit.
units.category: Media and language · headlines, sensational language and wordplay
learningObjectives: Read abbreviated headlines with omitted articles, prepositions or auxiliary verbs and present tense for past events.
Recognise ambiguity, alliteration and emotionally charged language used to attract readers.
Interpret dramatic militaristic verbs and informal labels with appropriate register awareness.
Identify double meanings in headline puns including shell-shocked, bad blood, hopping mad and round-up.

sectionsChecked: A · Features of headline language, exemplars and explanatory notes
B · Violent words, four illustrative headline patterns
C · Playing with words, headline puns and Language help
Exercises 100.1–100.3, including one-off pun headlines, and the answer key

items.pt: virar manchete; ganhar grande destaque nas notícias
items.section: A · Features of newspaper headline language
items.example: The discovery hit the headlines across the country.
items.note: An event suddenly attracts widespread news coverage, not simply appears in any article.

items.pt: jornal popular de estilo sensacionalista; tabloide
items.section: A · Features of newspaper headline language
items.example: The tabloid gave the celebrity scandal more space than the policy debate.
items.note: The unit contrasts popular dramatic headline style with ordinary prose; tabloid can also mean a newspaper format.

items.pt: manchete; título de notícia
items.section: A · Features of newspaper headline language
items.example: The headline left out several words that appeared in the full report.
items.note: News heading that summarises or attracts attention to a story; not all headlines are tabloids.

items.pt: linguagem de manchetes; estilo conciso de títulos jornalísticos
items.section: A · Features of newspaper headline language
items.example: Headline language often omits words that would be essential in a complete sentence.
items.note: A specialised reading register that should not generally be copied into normal writing or speech.

items.pt: omitir artigos
items.section: A · Features of newspaper headline language
items.example: Newspaper editors sometimes omit articles to fit a headline into limited space.
items.note: Headlines may omit a, an and the even when the full sentence needs them.

items.pt: omitir verbos auxiliares
items.section: A · Features of newspaper headline language
items.example: The headline omitted auxiliary verbs to make the message shorter.
items.note: Forms such as is, was or has are often dropped in headlines, unlike standard prose.

items.pt: presente simples usado em manchetes
items.section: A · Features of newspaper headline language
items.example: In headline present simple, a past event can be described as if it were happening now.
items.note: News headlines often choose present simple for recently completed actions to add immediacy.

items.pt: ambíguo; com mais de uma interpretação possível
items.section: A · Features of newspaper headline language
items.example: The ambiguous headline did not reveal whether cloud meant weather or online storage.
items.note: Ambiguity can draw readers in; it may be resolved only by reading the article.

items.pt: associação dramática; conotação de forte impacto
items.section: A · Features of newspaper headline language
items.example: The word disaster carries a dramatic association that makes the headline sound urgent.
items.note: Words chosen for emotional impact can distort the apparent significance of an event.

items.pt: revelar; divulgar
items.section: A · Features of newspaper headline language
items.example: The minister will reveal the proposal at a press conference tomorrow.
items.note: A short strong reporting verb often appearing in headlines; it does not guarantee the information is new.

items.pt: celebridade; pessoa famosa
items.section: A · Features of newspaper headline language
items.example: The tabloid featured a celebrity on its front page.
items.note: Well-known people are frequent headline subjects, particularly in tabloids.

items.pt: aliteração; repetição de sons consonantais iniciais
items.section: A · Features of newspaper headline language
items.example: The editor used alliteration to make the headline more memorable.
items.note: Repetition of the same initial sounds in neighbouring words, not necessarily identical letters.

items.pt: homem armado; atirador
items.section: A · Features of newspaper headline language
items.example: Police said that a gunman had fled before officers arrived.
items.note: Compact newspaper noun for an armed man; reports may need a more precise description in context.

items.pt: enlouquecido; fora de controle, em linguagem sensacionalista
items.section: A · Features of newspaper headline language
items.example: The headline called the attacker crazed before the facts were established.
items.note: Emotionally charged tabloid descriptor; can stigmatise and should not be treated as a medical diagnosis.

items.pt: alvo; pessoa visada
items.section: A · Features of newspaper headline language
items.example: The athlete became the target of repeated online threats.
items.note: In headlines, target can be a noun or verb; context determines whether someone was selected, threatened or attacked.

items.pt: valentão violento; agressor
items.section: B · Dramatic and militaristic headline vocabulary
items.example: Witnesses described the attackers as thugs, although their identities were unknown.
items.note: Strong disapproving label for a violent person; frequent in sensational reporting.

items.pt: arruaceiro; jovem de comportamento agressivo, em inglês britânico
items.section: B · Dramatic and militaristic headline vocabulary
items.example: Local residents complained about yobs vandalising the bus stop.
items.note: Informal British disapproving term for badly behaved, often young, people; may be stereotyping.

items.pt: brutamontes; arruaceiro grosseiro
items.section: B · Dramatic and militaristic headline vocabulary
items.example: The columnist referred to the disruptive football fans as louts.
items.note: Disapproving word for a rude or aggressive person, similar to yob but not necessarily young.

items.pt: esmagar; reprimir de forma contundente
items.section: B · Dramatic and militaristic headline vocabulary
items.example: The editorial said officials were trying to crush the protest movement.
items.note: Often metaphorical in headlines for defeat or suppression, not necessarily a literal crushing action.

items.pt: repressão rigorosa; operação de endurecimento
items.section: B · Dramatic and militaristic headline vocabulary
items.example: The government announced a crackdown on illegal dumping.
items.note: Stronger enforcement or punitive action; normally takes on before the problem targeted.

items.pt: reprimir com maior rigor; intensificar o combate a
items.section: B · Dramatic and militaristic headline vocabulary
items.example: The authorities promised to crack down on fraudulent ticket sellers.
items.note: Phrasal verb matching noun a crackdown on; separate two-word verb and one-word noun.

items.pt: sitiar; cercar; assediar insistentemente
items.section: B · Dramatic and militaristic headline vocabulary
items.example: Reporters besieged the actor outside the theatre after the premiere.
items.note: Literally surround a fortified place; figuratively crowd or persistently pursue someone.

items.pt: devastar; atravessar causando destruição
items.section: B · Dramatic and militaristic headline vocabulary
items.example: A powerful storm ripped through the coastal village overnight.
items.note: Strong vivid verb phrase for movement that causes widespread damage.

items.pt: explosão; estrondo
items.section: B · Dramatic and militaristic headline vocabulary
items.example: Residents reported a blast near the railway station.
items.note: Short dramatic noun frequent in headlines for an explosion, among other senses.

items.pt: discordância; oposição política; dissidência
items.section: B · Dramatic and militaristic headline vocabulary
items.example: Civil rights groups criticised the crackdown on dissent.
items.note: Formal term for public disagreement with an authority or dominant view.

items.pt: primeiro-ministro; sigla jornalística
items.section: B · Dramatic and militaristic headline vocabulary
items.example: The PM is expected to announce the changes on Thursday.
items.note: Headline abbreviation for prime minister; the initials should be read aloud individually.

items.pt: policiais; tiras, em linguagem informal
items.section: B · Dramatic and militaristic headline vocabulary
items.example: The headline said cops were investigating the break-in.
items.note: Informal plural for police officers; not suitable for most formal police reports.

items.pt: trocadilho; jogo de palavras
items.section: C · Puns, metaphor and wordplay in headlines
items.example: The article title relied on a play on words involving the singer's surname.
items.note: An expression designed to evoke two meanings or similar-sounding words at once.

items.pt: reinado de terror; período de opressão violenta
items.section: C · Puns, metaphor and wordplay in headlines
items.example: The historical account described a reign of terror under the dictatorship.
items.note: Reign refers to rule or control; the unit's headline exploits the identical sound of rain.

items.pt: chuva de terror; trocadilho com reinado de terror
items.section: C · Puns, metaphor and wordplay in headlines
items.example: The magazine called the disastrous storm a rain of terror.
items.note: Deliberate pun on reign of terror, used for an unusually dramatic rain-related headline; not an ordinary fixed expression.

items.pt: marcar um gol; chutar e fazer um gol
items.section: C · Puns, metaphor and wordplay in headlines
items.example: The striker shot a goal in the final minute of the match.
items.note: The unit uses shoot to explain a newspaper pun, but score a goal is generally the more usual wording.

items.pt: estrela cadente; pessoa em ascensão rápida, conforme o contexto
items.section: C · Puns, metaphor and wordplay in headlines
items.example: The singer was described as a shooting star after her sudden breakthrough.
items.note: Literally a meteor; in a headline the phrase can also evoke shooting in a sports story and a surname.

items.pt: é o fim de; acabou para
items.section: C · Puns, metaphor and wordplay in headlines
items.example: After repeated losses, some fans thought it was curtains for the team.
items.note: Informal idiom meaning someone or something is finished; exploited in a pun about Corinth.

items.pt: ressentimento; inimizade entre pessoas
items.section: C · Puns, metaphor and wordplay in headlines
items.example: There was bad blood between the two directors after the dispute.
items.note: Established figurative collocation for hostility; the source headline also hints at a vampire story.

items.pt: bons tempos; dias felizes
items.section: C · Puns, metaphor and wordplay in headlines
items.example: The reunion brought back memories of the happy days of childhood.
items.note: Read as an ordinary positive expression or as a questioning headline that ironises a supposedly pleasant period.

items.pt: profundamente abalado; em estado de choque
items.section: C · Puns, metaphor and wordplay in headlines
items.example: The community was shell-shocked by the unexpected closure.
items.note: Originally associated with trauma from shelling in war; the headline plays on an animal's shell.

items.pt: impressões equivocadas; falsas impressões
items.section: C · Puns, metaphor and wordplay in headlines
items.example: The advertisement created false impressions about the product's reliability.
items.note: Misleading beliefs; the pun exploits dental impressions, moulds of the teeth.

items.pt: assombração feliz; trocadilho com caça feliz
items.section: C · Puns, metaphor and wordplay in headlines
items.example: The local paper used happy haunting for a friendly ghost story.
items.note: Playful one-off headline evoking happy hunting and a ghost's haunting; not a routine idiom.

items.pt: furioso; possesso de raiva
items.section: C · Puns, metaphor and wordplay in headlines
items.example: She was hopping mad when she discovered the booking had been cancelled.
items.note: Informal idiom for extreme anger; the pun also draws on a toad's hopping movement.

items.pt: radiante de sucesso; empolgado com uma conquista
items.section: C · Puns, metaphor and wordplay in headlines
items.example: Flushed with success, the team announced another ambitious project.
items.note: Fixed figurative phrase for pride or excitement after a success; headline pun also refers to flushing a toilet.

items.pt: extremamente constrangido
items.section: C · Puns, metaphor and wordplay in headlines
items.example: He was highly embarrassed when the security alarm sounded during his speech.
items.note: Highly intensifies embarrassment; a headline plays additionally on literal height.

items.pt: reunião organizada; compilação; agrupamento, conforme o contexto
items.section: C · Puns, metaphor and wordplay in headlines
items.example: The newspaper published a weekly round-up of community news.
items.note: As a noun, a summary or collection; the exercise plays on the verb round up used for herding animals.

items.pt: reunir; juntar; arrebanhar animais
items.section: C · Puns, metaphor and wordplay in headlines
items.example: The farmer asked the dogs to round up the sheep before nightfall.
items.note: Two-word phrasal verb, distinct in form from noun round-up; also means gather people or objects.

items.pt: aparição; fantasma ou manifestação sobrenatural
items.section: C · Puns, metaphor and wordplay in headlines
items.example: Guests reported seeing an apparition near the old staircase.
items.note: In the exercise, it describes a ghost, enabling a pun with haunting.
